questions.q: In 'The Sheep and the Pig', why did the Pig squeal so much more than the Sheep would?
choices: The Shepherd wanted his bacon, not just wool
The Shepherd was squeezing him much too tightly
He was afraid the Sheep would laugh at him later
He wanted to stay in the meadow to eat more acorns
questions.evidence: When he catches you he is only after your wool. But he wants my bacon!

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Sheep and the Pig'?
choices: It is easy to be brave when there is no danger
Pigs will always make more noise than sheep do
Always stay in your own meadow and do not wander
Shepherds are always kind to the animals they keep
questions.evidence: It is easy to be brave when there is no danger.

questions.q: In 'The Travelers and the Purse', what did one traveler find on the road?
choices: A purse that seemed full of gold
A lost dog sitting by the road
A map that showed hidden treasure
A fresh loaf of bread in a basket

questions.q: In 'The Travelers and the Purse', why did the companion tell the finder to say "I am lost"?
choices: He would not share the purse, so he could not share the trouble
The companion wanted to keep the purse for himself in the end
The companion thought they were really lost on the wrong road
The companion was angry because he had not found it first
questions.evidence: You would not say 'we' before, so now stick to your 'I'.

questions.q: In 'The Lion and the Ass', what did the Lion do when the Ass made a scornful remark?
choices: He walked quietly on
He sprang and attacked the Ass
He roared back at him loudly
He turned and ran away in fear

questions.q: In 'The Frogs Who Wished for a King', what did Jupiter send the Frogs first?
choices: A huge log
A tall Crane
A fierce Lion
A big Fish
questions.evidence: he threw down a huge log

questions.q: In 'The Frogs Who Wished for a King', what did the Crane king do?
choices: Gobbled up the Frogs
Gave the Frogs a feast
Let the Frogs dive off him
Built the Frogs a new pond
questions.evidence: He gobbled up the poor Frogs right and left

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Frogs Who Wished for a King'?
choices: Be sure you can better your condition before you seek to change
A quiet log that never moves makes the very best kind of king
Always do exactly what Jupiter says and never ask him for more
Frogs should hide among the reeds and never leave their marsh
questions.evidence: Be sure you can better your condition before you seek to change.
